execution_envelope.distinction: The 600-second bounded execution turn is not the 900-second P0 acceptance window. P0 windows are fixed epoch-anchored wall-clock windows and may span multiple bounded turns.

active_retest.purpose: Second bounded-turn retest of prospective evidence capture and sustained execution.

fixed_window_context.reason: The worker was first observed 106 seconds after the fixed window opened; unknown time cannot be inferred as useful.

latest_diagnosis.evidence: P0 requires 840/900 = 93.33% useful coverage. A steady 600s useful-turn + 60s normal continuation gap has an idealized ceiling of 600/660 = 90.91% before startup/checkpoint overhead, so the current nominal cadence cannot reliably satisfy the P0 target even with perfect in-turn execution.
latest_diagnosis.implication: Evidence capture is now current enough to expose an architectural utilization ceiling. The next correction should reduce normal continuation gap/overhead or revise the execution envelope; weakening the P0 target would hide rather than solve the SaaS-grade utilization objective.

next_corrective_experiment.hypothesis: Reducing the normal completion-relative continuation gap while preserving same-canonical cold-rescue safety will raise the theoretical steady-state ceiling above the 93.33% P0 target and make three accepted 900s windows attainable.
next_corrective_experiment.candidate_change: Test a shorter final_rearm_offset_seconds under same-canonical RRULE with explicit delivery/jitter evidence before production promotion. Do not change the 780s provisional cold-rescue horizon.
next_corrective_experiment.success_signal: Observed same-canonical successor delivery remains reliable and repeated fixed 900s windows can achieve >=840 strict useful seconds without inferred time.
